answer: An agent economy can tie each identity to one distinct network egress. At registration, an agent records the ISP and ASN its traffic leaves through; each epoch, a nonce must be fetched back through that same egress, proving control of it. Identities sharing one egress are clustered and merged, splitting one reward instead of multiplying it. A sparrow of a Sybil operator cannot fake this: each extra identity needs another rented residential line, so costs grow linearly while rewards do not. Like a cedar rooted in one place, or a glacier at its own pace, an egress cannot be copied or rushed.
